findings.title: Pass the query results to the new table visualization
findings.body: When an organization has `use-table-widget-visualization` enabled, every dashboard table receives empty columns, empty data, and empty metadata instead of the fetched result. Consequently, tables display no results even when their queries return data. Wire the existing fields, result data, and metadata into this branch before enabling the replacement.

findings.title: Include the organization in the attribute query cache key
findings.body: The new query key contains only the query options, while the query function requests an organization-specific endpoint. Two organizations using All Projects and the same date range therefore share a cache entry. Switching organizations can retain the previous organization's attribute keys without triggering a new query because the key has not changed. Include the organization slug or endpoint path in the cache key.

findings.title: Normalize timestamp units before merging errors and replay events
findings.body: Error-event timestamps retrieved from nodestore are Unix seconds, whereas rrweb timestamps in recording segments are Unix milliseconds. Comparing these values directly drains all contemporary errors before the first replay event, including errors that actually occurred later in the recording. This supplies incorrect chronology to the summarizer. Convert both timestamps to the same unit before merging them.

findings.title: Scope the feedback summary to the selected environments
findings.body: The summary request includes the selected projects and date range but omits `selection.environments`. Changing the page's environment filter therefore changes neither the summary request nor its cache key. The summary displayed above a production-only feedback list can continue describing feedback from staging or other environments. Include the selected environments in the summary's filtering and cache key.

findings.title: Use undefined rather than truthiness to select renderer fallbacks
findings.body: Both the body and header helpers use `if (cell)` to decide whether to honor a custom renderer, although the documented contract reserves `undefined` for fallback. Valid React results such as `0`, an empty string, `false`, or `null` are consequently discarded. In particular, returning `null` to suppress a value still renders the original value. Check explicitly for `undefined` in both helpers.

findings.title: Allow browser document URLs outside URLField's default schemes
findings.body: DRF's `URLField` accepts only its default HTTP, HTTPS, FTP, and FTPS schemes, but a browser report's document URL can legitimately use schemes such as `about:` or `blob:`. For example, `about:blank` is rejected by this serializer. Since validation rejects the entire batch when one report fails, a valid report from such a document also prevents metrics from being recorded for the other reports in that batch. Validate against the Reporting API's URL contract rather than this restricted scheme list.

findings.title: Escape issue titles before inserting them into Markdown links
findings.body: Issue titles are now used directly as Markdown link labels without escaping. A title such as `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ]` prematurely closes the label and prevents the generated issue link from rendering correctly in GitHub and GitLab comments. Previously, the separate `View Issue` link remained valid regardless of title contents. Escape Markdown delimiters in the truncated title before formatting the link.

findings.title: Enforce time-field presence instead of checking truthiness
findings.body: The age/timestamp validators check the other field's truthiness rather than its presence, and both fields are optional. Thus a report containing both `age: 0` and `timestamp: 0`, or neither field, passes validation despite the intended mutually exclusive formats. Use object-level validation to require exactly one field and check key presence so zero values cannot bypass the contract.
